extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, prospective authors, journal editors, librarians, and readers seeking information about the journal
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the scope, indexing, editorial information, metrics, and controversies related to the academic journal 'Communications in Algebra'. Useful for evaluating the journal's fit, visibility, and editorial practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal scope / subject coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Covering algebra, including commutative algebra, ring theory, module theory, non-associative algebra (including Lie algebras and Jordan algebras), group theory, and algebraic geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should fall within these listed areas of algebra; suitability for the journal is determined by topical fit with these subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications in Algebra is a monthly peer-reviewed scientific journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles submitted to the journal are (nominally) subject to peer review before publication; peer review is the primary quality-control mechanism for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal publishes on a monthly schedule; authors and readers can expect regular monthly issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracting and indexing coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is abstracted and indexed in CompuMath Citation Index, Current Contents/Chemical, Earth, and Physical Sciences, Mathematical Reviews, MathSciNet, Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE), and Zentralblatt MATH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing in these databases affects discoverability, institutional recognition, and ease of citation tracking; presence in major indexes is an indicator of visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact factor
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the Journal Citation Reports, the journal has a 2022 impact factor of 0.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact factor is presented as a quantitative metric of citation-based influence for 2022; prospective authors or evaluators may use this alongside other metrics to assess journal influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial review policy — number of referee reports required
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher decided to increase the number of required referee reports per submission (a decision later cited in the editorial board's resignation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required number of referee reports per manuscript is an explicit editorial policy that affects review thoroughness and turnaround; changes to this number can materially affect the review process and editorial workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial governance and consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial board resigned en masse over decisions by the publisher to increase referee reports per submission and to remove the editor-in-chief without consulting the board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher practices regarding consultation with the editorial board and procedures for removing an editor-in-chief are governance criteria that affect trust in editorial independence and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction and integrity handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal published a paper ('Eight-dimensional octonion-like but associative normed division algebra' by Joy Christian) whose results would contradict Hurwitz's theorem if true; the paper was later retracted by the journal's editorial board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence of a retraction and associated notices (DOIs, Retraction Watch coverage) indicates the journal has mechanisms for retracting problematic work and that handling of mathematical integrity is a relevant evaluative factor for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial leadership / editor-in-chief
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor-in-chief is Scott Chapman (Sam Houston State University); Earl J. Taft (Rutgers University) was the founding editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about the editor-in-chief and founding editors helps evaluate leadership, editorial direction, and the journal's academic stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is published by Taylor & Francis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher's identity signals general publisher policies, business practices, and reputation which can influence submission decisions and expectations about editorial processes.
